  Input: A single integer n representing the size of the grid, followed by n strings each of length n representing the grid itself. The grid contains characters 'P' and '#'.

    6. Iterate over the grid to find the coordinates of the first and second 'P' and store them in (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) respectively.
    7. Define arrays dx and dy to represent movement directions (up, right, down, left).
    8. Define a constant INF as a large integer value.
    9. Initialize a 4D integer array dist with dimensions n x n x n x n, filling it with INF.
    10. Create a queue to perform a breadth-first search, starting with the initial positions of the two 'P's.
    11. Set the distance of the initial positions in dist to 0.
    12. While the queue is not empty, perform the following:
        a. Dequeue the front element to get the current positions of the two 'P's.
        b. For each of the four possible movement directions, calculate the new positions for both 'P's.
        c. If a new position is out of bounds or is an obstacle '#', revert to the previous position.
        d. If the new positions have a greater distance than the current positions plus one, update the distance and enqueue the new positions.
    13. Initialize ans to a large integer value.
    14. Iterate over all possible positions in the grid to find the minimum distance where both 'P's are at the same position.
    15. If ans is still equal to INF, set ans to -1.
    16. Print the value of ans.
]
